text:
Mira: FYI Vela reported a burst of 429s and huge tail latencies during a marketing blast around 15:10 UTC. They’re on a Dedicated pool (pool-id: vela-prod-eu), seeing sustained 400-500 QPS spikes from a campaign and the pool didn't scale enough.
Alex: Can you paste the sample timestamps / QPS curve? any error messages from our side or client-side backoff?
Mira: Pasting the short summary: baseline ~120 QPS, expected peak ~300 QPS but this run spiked to ~480 QPS for ~7m. Target utilization was set at 0.7. Pool currently 4 nodes (g4dn-type), avg CPU/GPU util hit ~95% and per-request latency P99 jumped to 3.2s -> 8.6s. Many 429s at the client.
Mira: Their autoscale config: min=2, max=8, scale_cooldown=300s, scale_policy=utilization. They say the pool never reached more than 5 nodes during the spike.
Julio: Hmm sounds like scale lag + high variance requests. Could be slow scale init or warmup. Do we have the node launch logs + gateway throttles? @eng_sre_bot can you pull scaling events for pool vela-prod-eu between 2026-03-14T15:05:00Z and 15:20:00Z? :eyes:
eng_sre_bot: Requested logs: scaling_events (vela-prod-eu) 15:04-15:22 UTC: [15:06 scale +1 -> 3 nodes], [15:09 scale +1 -> 4 nodes], [15:12 scale +1 -> 5 nodes], [15:19 scale +0 (rate-limited by quota/region)]. Average node init time 90s, container warmup ~45s.
Alex: That aligns — ramp was faster than our autoscaler could fully provision healthy capacity. Also check if there's any node failures/cordons that prevented new nodes being used.
Mira: I grabbed a short engine log snippet from their request window (scrubbed):
```
2026-03-14T15:11:33Z | serve| request_id=ab12 | model=redwood-v1 | latency=520ms | kv-hit=0
2026-03-14T15:11:34Z | serve| request_id=ab13 | model=redwood-v1 | latency=6.1s | queue_wait=3200ms
2026-03-14T15:12:10Z | serve| request_id=ab14 | model=redwood-v1 | latency=8.6s | error=429:overloaded
```
Mira: They also noticed bursty token-length variance — some requests were long context/gen combos which increased per-request GPU time.
Alex: Two angles: (1) autoscaler config needs to be more aggressive for this customer workload (lower scale_cooldown, higher max, smaller step ramp), (2) consider warm standby or burst capacity during known marketing windows. Also look at request shaping — can we apply tenant-level rate limit or queue depth to smooth spikes?
Support-L2: Vela is on a committed Dedicated plan but didn't opt for burst capacity. They also have strict SLA so we need to propose options.
Julio: Can we quantify required nodes? Rough calc: assume average effective throughput per node under mixed request sizes = 80 QPS at target latency. For a 480 QPS peak we’d need ~6 nodes at 0.8 util -> 480 / (80*0.8) ≈ 7.5 -> round up to 8 nodes. They had max=8 but autoscaler ramped slowly and cooldown prevented reaching 8 quickly enough.
Tara: Good to include a recommendation doc for them. Short action items: 1) Ask Vela to temporarily increase max nodes to 10 and lower scale cooldown to 120s for next campaign, 2) Offer a pre-warm window where we spin to target node count 10 minutes before campaign start, 3) Suggest configuring a soft rate limit at their API gateway to avoid client retries amplifying spikes.
Mira: I've sent the initial postmortem to Vela with Julio's calc and Tara's options. They asked for repro steps so they can demonstrate locally to their team. Here’s a minimal repro curl sequence to mimic bursty client behavior (adapted):
```
# single-host parallel bursts (replace API_KEY & ENDPOINT)
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"long-prompt ...","max_tokens":512}' &
  if (( i % 50 == 0 )); then sleep 0.5; fi
done
wait
```
Mira: They ran something similar in staging and could reproduce 429s when pool nodes < 6.
Alex: Next diagnostic: capture per-node tail latency and kernel utilization during a controlled burst. If noisy neighbor (one workload hogging GPU memory/SMs) occurs, we’ll see imbalance across nodes. Also check if KV cache warms per-node causing initial slow requests on new nodes.
Julio: I’ll pull per-node GPU metrics and the per-instance request distribution. Also checking for any rate-limit errors in the control plane (quota exhaustion with our autoscaler requests).
Support-L2: For the customer-facing reply we should include: a) explanation of autoscaler behaviour and limits, b) recommended config changes with numbers (min/max/cooldown), c) offer pre-warm/burst add-on and runbook for marketing campaigns, and d) temporary mitigation steps (set soft rate limit, add client-side exponential backoff jitter).
Mira: I'll draft the reply and include a small bill impact note — if they increase max nodes or enable burst, it changes monthly committed cost.
Tara: Also flag product: maybe a "campaign pre-warm" feature to automate warming to a specified target at scheduled times. File a ticket with eng-runtime.
Alex: Agreed. For immediate triage, can we set a one-off manual scale to 9 nodes for Vela next campaign? If approvals OK, I’ll run it and monitor.
Mira: Vela approved the one-off. Alex, please do the manual scale and post back metrics in this thread. :thumbsup:
eng_sre_bot: Manual scale initiated by Alex at 2026-03-14T16:02:10Z -> target=9 nodes, expected ready ~6m.
Mira: Thanks all — recording action items and will follow up with the customer after we verify the next campaign.
